methodology:
BrasilAgro publicly discloses its property portfolio with farm names, hectares, and acquisition dates — making it possible to build a per-farm FMV table directly from filings. The 9 named farms shown below total ~498K acres (~78% of total ~625K acre portfolio); remaining post-2014 acquisitions are aggregated.

Three real-world data points anchor the FMV analysis:
1. Deloitte third-party appraisal of the entire portfolio at R$3.5B (June 2025) — the cleanest external mark
2. Chaparral Farm sale: 37,183 ha for R$364.5M (March 2024) = ~R$9,800/hectare = ~R$3,970/acre
3. Preferência Farm sale: 17,799 ha for R$141.4M (June 2025) = ~R$7,940/hectare = ~R$3,213/acre
4. Original company strategy is acquire → develop → sell: documented appreciation from acquisition cost to sale prices over 5-15 year hold periods

Per-region FMV anchors (all 2024-2025):
- Western Bahia (LEM): R$8,500-10,000/acre — Jatobá, Parceria I
- Northeast Matopiba (PI/TO): R$5,500-7,500/acre — Cremaq, Parceria II
- Mato Grosso sugarcane (mill-supply): R$11,500/acre — Alto Taquari residual
- Goiás sugarcane: R$11,000/acre — Araucária
- Minas Gerais forestry: R$3,500/acre — Nova Buriti

The R$3.5B Deloitte mark / 252K hectares = ~R$5,580/acre weighted is the portfolio-level reality check. My per-farm aggregation totals slightly above the Deloitte mark, reflecting more granular per-region pricing than a single-portfolio-average appraisal.
